### Findings

- Claude’s OAuth session expired, and the CLI could not refresh it. Reauthentication is required; this is not an md² execution failure. Anthropic documents `/login` as the interactive authentication flow. [Claude Code setup](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/getting-started)
- md² passes the raw Claude error into the conversation without classifying it as an authentication problem. [agent_provider_protocol.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_provider_protocol.js:90)
- Runs validate the account directory but not its login status. [agent_runner_service.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:247)
- The required recovery mechanism already exists. Account management runs `claude auth status` and opens a visible `claude /login` process using the correct account environment. [agent_account_service.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_account_service.js:180)

### Proposed solution

When a Claude turn fails with an authentication error, confirm the selected account with the existing status check. If login is required, show: “Claude sign-in expired. Log in again, then retry the action,” with a **Log in** button that invokes the existing account login workflow.

This avoids fragile error-text replacement, avoids checking authentication before every run, and requires no new terminal-launch implementation. No files were changed.

I think there is a serious bug in the system regarding the editing and saving of regular markdown files.

I opened the markdown file through the link on a conversation on an action popup. then changed some things to the file. I think i clicked on it again from within the action popup, closed it, opened some other markdown files, including the card that triggered the generation of the markdown file I edited.

In the ui everything looked ok, but the agent reported it could no longer find the file.

I closed and reopened the project and now the file was gone, but we had 2 duplicates of the card file. so something went seriously wrong her. perhaps in the save or commit process of the markdown editor in listview

## Current state

Regular Markdown files and cards use the same lifetime-stable `CardEditor`. The editor stores the active target separately from the Markdown editor instance. During a document switch, it flushes the outgoing content, changes the active target, and then replaces the editor content.

The programmatic replacement can still produce editor change callbacks after the active target changed. `handleEditorChange` applies every callback to the current target, not the target that initiated the change. Rapid reopen, close, and document switches can therefore apply one document's content to another document. The normal save pipeline then persists the corrupted in-memory document at its target path.

Existing tests cover ordinary switching and saving, but not delayed rich-editor callbacks across the reported open-edit-reopen-close-switch sequence.

## implementation details

* Make a list-editor document switch one transaction. Flush the outgoing target before starting the replacement and do not activate the incoming target until its expected Markdown is established as the editor baseline.
* Ignore programmatic and stale editor change callbacks while a replacement is pending. A callback may update a draft only when it belongs to the active document generation.
* Preserve the current document-specific history behavior and clear the pending switch state after success, discard, or failure.
* Reject a persistence batch containing multiple writes or moves to the same target path. Report the conflict instead of relying on write order.
* Add real `MDXEditor` regression coverage for regular Markdown and card documents. Exercise repeated link activation, editing, closing, reopening, and switching in the reported order, including a callback arriving after a switch.

## acceptance criteria

* Editing a regular Markdown file and then opening or closing other Markdown files never changes another document's draft or persisted content.
* Reopening the same file through a conversation link does not duplicate its tab, reset its pending edit, or redirect later changes to another document.
* Every editor callback is ignored or applied to the document generation that owns it; stale callbacks cannot modify the current document.
* Closing or switching away from a dirty document persists its latest content exactly once at its own path.
* Persistence fails visibly before writing when a batch contains the same target path more than once.
* Reopening the project shows the same files and contents that were visible after the last successful save, without missing files or duplicate cards.

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
